statement: A guard that runs every regex literal against adversarial input proves those regexes are linear. It proves nothing about the reader that calls them. A recursive expansion is bounded only by a budget on its total work. Incident: cejel #648 at b9762e0a3. Commit d5ff81601 said the v27 A1 run readers stay linear because the ReDoS guard passed (1,180 literals, 0 failures). An adversarial review then measured the hatch script reader at 15.4 s on a 328-byte hatch.toml (t = ["t", ...] sixty times; depth < 4 bounded depth, not width, so the work grew about as n^4), and the make expansion at 1.8 s on a 4.8 KB Makefile (a chain of empty references; the 4,096-character output cap never tripped). Fix: 33cd9508b shares a 4,096-substitution budget per Makefile and a 256-expansion budget per scan for hatch, and past either names the run as not read. Rule: before claiming a reader is linear, state the input that maximises its work and time it; a depth limit or an output cap is not a work bound.
